canonical_name: Continuous image of a connected subset is connected
literal_source_claim_en: The continuous image of a connected set is connected.
canonical_statement: For topological spaces X and Y, a subset E of X, and a globally continuous map f from X to Y, if E is nonempty and connected then its set-theoretic image f(E) is nonempty and connected.
canonical_claim: A continuous map sends every nonempty connected subset to a nonempty connected image.
statement_blocker: Master acceptance of the provisional exact target, minimal import, expression/environment fingerprints, transports, mutations, and boundary evidence remains open; intake predecessor acceptance and H0 historical-source fidelity are separate open gates.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: forall {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [TopologicalSpace alpha] [TopologicalSpace beta] {s : Set alpha}, IsConnected s -> forall f : alpha -> beta, Continuous f -> IsConnected (f '' s)

domain_and_universes: Candidate scope: arbitrary universe-polymorphic types alpha and beta with arbitrary topological-space structures; a subset s of alpha; and a total function f : alpha -> beta considered only on s. Exact universe and implicit-instance serialization remains downstream.
quantifiers: for every pair of topological spaces alpha and beta
for every subset s of alpha
for every function f from alpha to beta
hypotheses: s is nonempty and preconnected, represented by IsConnected s
f is globally continuous, represented by Continuous f
conclusion: The direct set image f '' s is connected, represented by IsConnected (f '' s).
